configMerge: Provider is the conversation provider when present; for a new conversation it inherits a valid saved apiChat.defaultModel provider first, otherwise personalKnowledge.apiChatProvider (default openai-compatible).
Configured profiles retain order; a remembered profile participates only when its saved provider and id match the conversation selection, and is appended only when its id is absent.
Legacy ids are considered in order: personalKnowledge.aiModel (default gpt-4o-mini), apiChatModels, then the conversation profile id; known configured profiles win by id.
Original selection guards reject a model if any configured alias sharing its model/deployment string is deprecated.
An unlisted HTTP model id becomes status unknown with a conservative 4096 context / 1024 output-token profile; this is not evidence that the remote model exists.
The HTTP API credential is read natively from SecretStorage key personalKnowledge.aiApiKey; the isolated adapter only consumes an injected opaque handle and never retrieves or returns a value.
Azure uses aiAzureApiVersion (default 2024-06-01); endpoints and API versions are never included in public output.

vscode: Original profile id is vscode:<encoded vendor>:<encoded model id>; label is model name plus vendor.
Context window comes from maxInputTokens; output tokens are min(positive maxOutputTokens or 4096, floor(maxInputTokens / 4)).
Native imageInput is true only when the provider reports that capability.
The isolated server does not discover VS Code or Copilot SDK models; it reports discovery unsupported and returns no synthetic native model.
providerMetadata.http: Configured API profile metadata comes from apiChatModelProfiles; API model id/deployment entries not present there retain the legacy unknown 4096/1024 profile.

tokenAccounting.verifiedFormula: API model estimate starts at 32; for each message add UTF-8 bytes of content plus JSON.stringify(tool_calls) when present, then add 32.
tokenAccounting.excluded: VS Code model token counts use the native model tokenizer when available and are intentionally not emulated by this host-neutral adapter.

integration.constructor: new ModelConfigService({ configuration, secretResolver, registryAvailability, now? })
integration.configuration: Explicit allowlisted personalKnowledge settings plus optional rememberedModel snapshot; no process.env or host configuration reads.
integration.secretResolver: resolveSecret('personalKnowledge.aiApiKey') returns an opaque object handle or undefined; raw strings are rejected as credentials.
integration.registryAvailability: Parent-injected provider registry booleans; false means provider-unavailable. VS Code model discovery remains unsupported regardless.
integration.definitions: Import modelConfigDefinitions from src/model-config.ts and register its two read-only model.config.catalog/model.config.resolve schemas.
integration.transport: No HTTP client, model transport, or network request is injected or invoked. Tests use metadata-only registry booleans and inert opaque-secret fixtures; real model/transport fixtures are intentionally excluded.
